item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
How about:

Addendum: Notes Following Testing

During a series of extensive testing of the effects of various illumination sources on SCP-280's retreat reflex, SCP-280 broke containment. SCP-280 was observed to repeatedly appear and dissipate throughout the illuminated Site, progressing through the sub-levels and eventually appearing in SCP-1591's containment chamber. Upon being exposed to SCP-1591, SCP-280 displayed its eyes but did not retreat. The entity paused and knelt for several minutes before demanifestation. SCP-280 reappeared in its cell several hours later without incident.

This has more to do with giving some character to 280 (due to 1591's endnote/WL tale), than a simple light-skip crosstest (though it's that as well).

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Fair enough.

A big factor to this article is how hard it is to contain 280 due to the effects light has on it, and so the angle I was trying to take was an anomalous light source altering 280's usual behavior. Fighting ghosts with yet more ghosts seemed a humorous means of doing that, IMO.

I'll see if I can find something more suitable.

So here we have an article about a ghost-like/boogyman-like creature that runs from light. My immediate thought is, surely at some point the Foundation tested the effects of different light sources on the anomaly, even if this was done accidentally in defense during a containment breach. As it so happens, we have an anomalous light source in the form of the Ghostlight, aka SCP-2176. So, what happens when you use ghost powered illumination against a creepy specter like SCP-280? I propose the following addendum:

Addendum: Notes Following Testing

During a series of extensive testing of the effects of various illumination sources on SCP-280's retreat reflex, it was observed that the light generated by SCP-2176 caused a slower and more gradual dissipation of SCP-280 than other illumination sources. It is unknown if this change in behavior is due to SCP-2176's illumination source, or additional factors. Further testing involving SCP-2176 pending.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!
